diagnostics.message: signalfx_aws_integration.integration is created without waiting for aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration (the SplunkObservabilityPolicy inline policy) to be attached to the role. The graph only gives it an implicit dep on aws_iam_role.splunk_integration (via role_arn) and an explicit dep on time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, and that sleep depends only on the role — so the policy can still be attaching after the integration is created. The Splunk Observability provider docs for signalfx_aws_external_integration explicitly say role-related resources created by Terraform must be added as dependencies of signalfx_aws_integration for correct ordering/cleanup, and that the role needs the permissions (e.g. cloudwatch:* for use_metric_streams_sync, iam:PassRole) when the integration is created and validated. Add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration to signalfx_aws_integration.integration's depends_on.

signalfx_aws_integration.integration does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy (SplunkManagedMetricStreams), which grants the cloudwatch:*MetricStream* and iam:PassRole permissions the integration needs because it sets use_metric_streams_sync = true and enable_check_large_volume = true. Nothing in the graph orders that policy attachment before the integration is created (time_sleep only waits on the role), so Splunk Observability Cloud may attempt to validate/start metric streams against a role that doesn't yet have those permissions. Per the provider docs, role-related resources must be listed in signalfx_aws_integration's depends_on; add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy there.
